findings.proposed_text:
Exit criteria: the criteria this step covers (listed above) are this action's exit criteria.
(1) Before editing, note each criterion's check (its `Confirm by:` method when given) and what passes. Tests, check scripts, fixtures, golden files and thresholds are checks: change them only when a criterion says to.
(2) Confirm with what is present; never download, install or fetch a tool or dependency to confirm. Record the best evidence and what would confirm the rest.
(3) Stay within the item: if passing a check would make the result do or claim more than the item asks, leave it failing and report the discrepancy.
(4) After your last edit, rerun every check in one pass; only that pass counts. On a failure change the work, not the check, and rerun all.
(5) Stop on exactly one: all confirmed or inspected (or `unconfirmable` where the plan says `Confirm by: unconfirmable here`) and none failed -> done; a criterion proven unachievable (it contradicts another criterion, the item or a protected file after all compatible work, keeping existing behaviour at the conflict; it needs an absent tool, access or authority; or it exceeds the item) -> revise naming it (blocked with blocked_by only when a person, grant or outside dependency must act); the same check failing after 3 genuine fixes -> revise with it failed.
Report each criterion's check, final-pass output and level (confirmed, inspected, failed, not_run, unconfirmable), plus discrepancies, in the summary or a linked note.
findings.risk: Low: all obligations kept.

findings.proposed_text:
Exit criteria: the criteria this step covers (listed above) are this action's exit criteria.
(1) Before editing, note each criterion's check (its `Confirm by:` method when given) and what passes. Tests, check scripts, fixtures, golden files and thresholds are checks: change them only when a criterion says to.
(2) Confirm with what is present; never download, install or fetch a tool or dependency to confirm. Record the best evidence and what would confirm the rest.
(3) Stay within the item: if passing a check would make the result do or claim more than the item asks, leave it failing and report the discrepancy.
(4) After your last edit, rerun every check in one pass; only that pass counts. On a failure change the work, not the check, and rerun all.
(5) Stop on exactly one: all confirmed or inspected (or `unconfirmable` where the plan says `Confirm by: unconfirmable here`) and none failed -> done; a criterion proven unachievable (it contradicts another criterion, the item or a protected file after all compatible work, keeping existing behaviour at the conflict; it needs an absent tool, access or authority; or it exceeds the item) -> revise naming it (blocked with blocked_by only when a person, grant or outside dependency must act); the same check failing after 3 genuine fixes -> revise with it failed.
Report each criterion's check, final-pass output and level (confirmed, inspected, failed, not_run, unconfirmable), plus discrepancies, in the summary or a linked note.
findings.risk: Low: all obligations kept.

cross_cutting: Stage-critical operation lines are rendered at the END of the full packet (Step line for implement, Until Loop Start/receipt/command list for test-green/regression, Expected-RED list for test-red, Test rerun list for test-refine, lint command for implement), but packet_head prints only callback, goal, Done-when, Checked-by, Considerations and the ~1.8k result template. The model opened 1 of 22 packet files and grepped two; move these lines into packet_head, ahead of the result template.

The model piped `complete` output through `| head -c 1800..4000`, cutting heads mid-template; ordering the head as callback > goal/done/checked > stage operation lines > result template > 'Full packet:' path would keep the operative part within the first ~1.5k.
Baseline and test-author never print the recorded test commands or case IDs that their Done-when and Checked-by refer to; stage_commands() already computes them.

Each packet carries ~3.7k of shared-core text that is either inapplicable to inner stages (workspace return/handoff block, Improve 'advances directly' lines, contrary to the 2026-10-10 owner rule) or duplicated within the packet (accepted-source blocks vs 'Results this stage builds on', callback twice, Repeatable test-suite guide twice).
COMMON's requirement-definition paragraphs (~1.9k) ride in execution-only stages (baseline, test-red, test-green, regression).
Code craft (3.7k) is attached to test-red, whose packet says 'Do not edit product code'; test-author needs only its test-code subset.
CASE_END_STATES offers 'replan', which no inner stage allows.
The same rule is stated 3-5 times inside one packet: 'fail inside a test' (test-red x4), lint gate (implement x5, test-green x3), 'change a check only for an independent reason' (test-refine x3).

The Until Loop instructions never forbid a prewritten or scripted done payload; both loop stages produced trivial passes from canned JSON or loop.sh. TEST_ITERATION step 2 makes a trivial pass legitimate when nothing failed, so the gap is evidence provenance, not the pass itself.

Retry caps in implement and test-refine ('3 genuine fix attempts -> revise') and test-green/regression ('7 refused runs -> revise') may conflict with the owner memory 'ShipLoop loops unbounded'; noted, not proposed for change here.
